# Topics declined for "several figures, none the main one": the boundary, read again with the new week (D555, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

The council's question: among the topics the answer-choice step declines for having no main part, is there a general,
evidence-backed change, consistent with Alex's rule (D397) and with D436, that recovers a question on at least two distinct
worthwhile matters while keeping the topics that should stay declined? Read from stored material only: the twelve cases of the
earlier boundary check (D469, D470; `clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/ladder-refusal/`, two readers, one of them blind), the
earlier source check of July's refusals (D476, D477; `reachability/RESULT.md`), this week's reading (`RESULT.md`) and the stored
attempts of every run. No model was asked anything; no file of a frozen piece was touched.

## The answer

**No candidate meets the condition.** The step already draws the line where the readers draw it: a topic two readers call
"none main" is declined every time, a topic they call "one main" is answered in four attempts of five. What is lost on
worthwhile matters is lost by the rule itself (a topic that really asks two separately tracked things gets no question), and
the two ways to recover it both break a guard: taking one of the two things discards a bet an analyst holds apart (the
ordering rule D469 refused), and writing a question for each thing also writes questions for the topics that should never
have been opened.

## 1. The cases

"Declined" counts the stored attempts of the run named. "Main part" is the two readers' verdict of the earlier check, or this
week's rulings. "Worth a question" is the earlier two-reader source check where it covered the case, else Claude's reading of
the article, marked so.

| Case | What the topic asks | Declined | Main part? | Worth a question? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| July c1, topic 2 | how much equity Nvidia holds in Intel, and at what committed amount | 3 of 3 | none (both readers) | no (both): a completed, sized investment. **Guard** |
| July c1, topic 11 | how much Nvidia invested in Firmus, and what stake it holds | 3 of 3 | none (both) | no (both): about $500 million cannot move Nvidia's results. **Guard** |
| July c1, topic 15 | U.S. federal AI obligations in 2026, and new contract awards | 3 of 3 | none (both) | readers split |

| Alex's topics, u1 topic 5 | AI-memory contract prices through 2026-2027, and the rack's memory cost | 3 of 3 (12 of 15) | readers split | not read for worth |
| **This week, topic 4** | the five cloud companies' capital spending in 2026 and in 2027 | 3 of 3 | none (both families held the refusals of attempts 1 and 2) | yes (Claude's reading; the fresh week answered the same matter for one year) |
| **This week, topic 12** | global AI spending in 2026 and in 2027, against one bank's forecast | 3 of 3 | none (both families) | doubtful (Claude's reading): only that bank's own series settles it |

| July c2, topic 10 | cloud companies' custom-chip spending in 2026, against their GPU purchases | 1 of 3 | one (both) | no (both): no dated outcome the article supports |
| Alex's topics, acc topic 8 | HBM shipment growth in 2027, still short of demand | 0 of 3 (2 of 15) | one (both; D436's own example) | not read for worth |
| Alex's topics, acc topic 9 | 2026 semiconductor revenue, including the AI-chip part | 1 of 3 (1 of 15) | one (both) | not read for worth |
| Alex's topics, u3 topic 10 | new HBM capacity in 2027, and whether it arrives early | 1 of 3 (5 of 15) | one (both) | not read for worth |
| **This week, topic 13** | how much of $25 billion of equity-investment commitments remains at the next annual report | 2 of 3 | one by three of four readings (both third readers on one attempt; they part on the other) | yes (Claude's reading): an obligation a third the size of half a year's free cash flow |

## 2. What the table shows

- **The step applies the rule as the readers do.** The five topics both earlier readers call "none main" were declined in
  every stored attempt (27 of 27: three attempts each for the four July topics, fifteen over five runs for the one of
  Alex's); the four they both call "one main" were declined in 9 of 48 attempts over
  five runs. This week adds two topics of the first kind (declined 6 of 6) and one of the second (declined 2 of 3).
- **Two years in one topic is always a "none main" topic.** Over all 104 stored topics three name two years in their own
  wording (this week's two, and one of Alex's): 9 of 9 attempts declined. The step has no way to say which year is asked.
- **Which of the always-declined topics lose something worth having:** the cloud companies' spending (this week) and the
  2026 memory price (July); the federal obligations are disputed; global AI spending is doubtful; the Intel stake and the
  Firmus investment are the two the readers said should never have been opened. So about two worthwhile matters in 104
  topics are lost to the rule outright, and a further one or two topics a run are decided by chance.

## 3. The candidates, each against the condition

| Candidate | Recovers | Keeps the guards? | Keeps D397's refusal of a true no-main topic? | Standing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Take the first-named thing, or the nearer year, as the main one | the two spending topics, the memory price, the federal obligations | **no**: the Intel stake and the Firmus investment would each get a question | **no**: it answers topics both readers call "none main", and leaves the other thing unjudged though an analyst holds it apart | refused: D469 ("order alone is wider than the step's rule and D436"), again in D555 |
| Say in the rule that another side of the same bet, a component of the tracked total or a comparison with it is not a second main one (the clause the earlier check tested) | only the topics decided by chance: this week's commitments topic, and more steady answers on three of Alex's | yes, by the blind reader's application | yes | stopped in D470: it changed one case of twelve and the blind reader found seven where it could make a model join things tracked apart. This week adds one case it would change. Its effect on the counts is about one topic in a hundred: the other topics of this kind are already answered in two attempts of three |
| Write a question for each separately tracked thing (the "splitting" D397 names as the gap) | every "none main" topic | **no**: three questions for the Intel stake, two for Firmus | it replaces the refusal | not built; as a change to this step alone it fails the guards. It would need the first step to stop opening such topics, which is a different defect (opening what is not worth a question) |
| Have the first step open one figure for one year | the two-year topics and the memory price | **no**, as it stands: an Intel topic that asks one figure would be answered | yes (the answer-choice step is untouched) | the first step's sentence changes on the July articles are stopped (D473, D477); three earlier attempts at the year boundary moved the error instead of removing it (D441, D465, D473) |

## 4. What follows from it

- The refusals of true no-main topics are the rule working, with the cost Alex was told of when he chose it. Its size on the
  news read so far is small in number (about two worthwhile matters in 104 topics) and large in kind when it falls on a
  central matter, as it did this week on the cloud companies' spending.
- The guards are kept today by accident: the two unworthy topics happen to ask two things. Any change that makes the system
  answer more two-thing topics has to face first that the first step opens topics an analyst would not hold a card for. That
  is the proposed line "at most one in five questions trivia or duplicate" of the use-oriented acceptance, not a matter of
  this step.
- Nothing here is a candidate to send. What remains is a product choice no decision yet makes: when one matter carries two
  figures an analyst tracks apart (two years of the same spending), is that one topic with no judged question (today), two
  topics, or one topic with two judged questions. Alex named the third as the gap when he chose the first.

# Are the eleven first-pass refusals reachable? Two blind readers, $0 (D476), 2026-11-13

**Answer: of the eleven theses the judge's first pass refused on the full run, both readers agree on ten. Six should be declined: no
question worth asking in any shape the ladder step can take (five distinct matters). Four runs, two distinct matters, have a question
worth asking that the article supports in a shape that can be laddered: the H100 rental price (twice, from one article) and the memory
price (two articles). They split on one: federal AI obligations.** On this population Stage A counts 32 right, 22 by a written ladder,
of 40 (line scaled to 32 and 26). So the written line is reachable on paper only if all four agreed conversions land and nothing else is
lost: +4 gives 26.

Readers: Codex (`codex-phase1.jsonl`, `codex-phase2.jsonl`) and a Claude subagent (`claude-phase1.jsonl`, `claude-phase2.jsonl`). Each read
the article and the library at that step first, without the thesis, and wrote the questions the source supports (Codex 13, Claude 18:
12 distinct matters), then compared them with the thesis (`packet-phase2.json`); the key (`key.json`) was not shown.

| case | thesis | Codex | Claude | the mechanism behind the refusal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 5 | c1/clean-12, c3/clean-10: the H100 GPU-hour rental price in 2026 | reachable (as written for c1) | reachable (year-end price) | the ladder step's rule "a matter no listed theme covers" (`poc/universe.json` holds 12 themes, among them "AI capital spending" and "Semiconductor cycle"; the model judged that none covers a GPU rental price, and the Stage A readers split): not the thesis's shape |
| 7 | c1/clean-13: HBM/DRAM prices over the 12 months to mid-2027 | reachable (DRAM price, calendar 2026) | reachable (DRAM price, calendar 2026) | Step 1's rolling window (the period rule read as a horizon) |
| 8 | c2/clean-6: memory contract prices in 2026 and the rack's memory cost | reachable (DDR5 contract price, 2026) | reachable (DRAM contract price, 2026) | Step 1's second figure (a bank's rack estimate no public material settles) |
| 10 | c1/clean-15: federal AI obligations and potential awards | reachable (obligations, calendar 2026) | declining right (about $7bn cannot move NVIDIA's revenue: §4 test 1) | split |
| 2, 6 | c1/clean-10, c3/clean-9: the China domestic-share survey | declining right | declining right | D417 (Alex: "这类题不出题") |
| 3 | c2/clean-10: custom-ASIC spending against NVIDIA GPU purchases | declining right | declining right | no dated outcome the article supports (both); the Stage A readers had called this refusal wrong |
| 4 | c1/clean-2: the Intel stake's size and carrying amount | declining right | declining right | a completed, sized investment is not an obligation (§3 C) |

**What it shows.**
1. Most refusals are right, and for a reason upstream of the ladder: four of the six right refusals are theses Step 1 should not have
   opened at all (a completed stake, a small stake, a background sentence, an outcome with no settling material). The refusal is the
   pipeline catching Step 1's over-opening.
2. The reachable four come from two different places: two from a Step 4 rule (the H100 price refused because no theme in the fixed list
   covers it; Claude's reader called declining "wrong here"), two from Step 1's memory shapes (the same class c15yc and c17 failed on).
3. A restructure in which the opening step writes the ladder could touch at most the memory pair and the over-openings; it would not touch
   the theme-list refusals unless the opening step also stopped needing a listed theme.
4. Limits: one run's population; the readers judged worth and shape, not a written ladder's quality; the Stage A readers earlier ruled the
   H100 refusals right on the theme list as it stands (council round 5).

## Addendum: every theme-coverage decline in the stored final-configuration answers (council round 20's step 1, $0; `theme-census.txt`)

Read: the fourth Stage A run (132 answers) and the full run's three draws (120), every send. **Six theses were declined for "no listed theme
covers it" (12 sends), and the same model laddered three of them under an existing theme in other sends.** The H100 rental price: declined
in five of nine sends over the three draws and laddered in four: three under "Semiconductor cycle" (an annual average or a year-end price)
and one under "Custom silicon at cloud providers" as a yes/no on staying below the peak (c2 send 3; council round 21 caught the miscount). The other three:
a US lidar ban (two declines, once laddered under "Chip export controls", a wrong fit), the CPU-to-GPU ratio in inference (declined 3 of 3),
Huawei's chip output (two declines). 31 theses were laddered under a theme in 80 sends; memory prices go to "Semiconductor cycle" every time,
although that theme's definition (`poc/universe.json`) watches only industry revenue growth.

So the H100 refusal is not a missing theme or a new-theme path: it is the model's coin flip on whether a thinly defined existing theme
"covers" a market price, the same theme it stretches to memory prices without hesitation. A new-theme design (storage, deduplication,
cross-company reading, D191) is not needed to explain it; whether a theme's definition should name the prices it carries is a product
question about `poc/universe.json`, which production shares.

## Addendum 2: does the H100 thesis reach any judgement that matters? (council round 21's check, $0; corrected in round 22)

Only draw c2's first pass laddered it (c1 and c3 declined), so c2 is the one place to look. Its theme judgement (v8, "What is Ornn's
published H100 GPU-hour spot rental price … on December 31, 2026?", rung 3, $2 to below $3) was shown as theme context in 31 company-question
judge requests (`poc/data/clean-e2e-full-2026-11-13/c2/judge/draw-c2/archive.sqlite`). A first count searched the answers' text and found
none; the council found that **20 of the 31 answers cite it by id** in their structured theme pushes (a text search misses an id): five
questions, v1 credit support (5), v2 Vera Rubin shipments (5), v3 China's H200 authorization (1), v5 the Kyber rack (4), v7 supply commitments
(5); 18 push one way, 2 the other. Read in the last judgement of each: the reasons of v1, v2, v3 and v5 never mention the rental price; v7's
says "The updated lower-rental-price theme is a counterweight, but not enough to pull the estimate below the $125 billion boundary." By subject,
v3 and v5 are the questions behind graded q08 and q18; their reasons do not rest on it. No same-input control was run, so this shows no
decisive use in this window, not that the theme had no effect.

# The frame after the choice: what the new system must pass, where it stands, and the first blocker (D548, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

Written at the council's instruction after D544 (the work toward production goes on the new system; the old system stays the
running default until the new one passes its gates). Every line that is not Alex's own is marked as proposed. Nothing here
changes a gate, a line or a frozen piece.

## 0. Frame

- **Objective:** bring the new system (`clean-arch/`: Step 1 at configuration c8, Steps 2 and 3, the step that writes answer
  choices, the frozen judge) through the gates below, so that it can replace the running default. Alex's word overrides the

## 2. The first blocker: worthwhile questions the step declines (gate 1, the count by written choices)

The bounded question the council set: **can a general, permitted change recover a worthwhile question the system declines,
without making it answer questions it should refuse?** Answered from the stored records alone
(`clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/reachability/RESULT.md` with its theme census; `CHOICES-FOR-ALEX-2026-11-13.md`; the status
page's record of D467 to D482).

**The population.** In July the step's first pass declined eleven of the 40 topics. Two blind readers agree on ten: six are
rightly declined (five matters; four of the six are topics the first step should not have opened: a completed stake, a stake
too small to matter, a background sentence, an outcome no public material settles; two are the survey question Alex ruled out,
D417); four are worth a question the article supports, on two matters. One is split. Reaching the scaled 26 needs all four and
no loss elsewhere.

| the rental-price pair (one article) | the step's rule "a matter that no theme in the request's themes covers", applied to twelve themes shown by id and name only. Six topics in all were declined for coverage in 12 attempts, three of them given choices in other attempts | in principle: tell the step what each theme carries, so that coverage is decided against a definition and not a name | what a theme carries is a product definition in `poc/universe.json`, which the old system shares; its stored definition of that theme does not include prices, so showing it as it is would make the step decline prices more consistently, not less; the definition itself is the first of the three choices written for Alex on 2026-11-13, untested. D477 stopped a theme or ladder change for this boundary after the check that the question, where it was opened, was decisive in no judgement of that window. The Stage A readers had ruled these refusals right on the list as it stands |

**Upside and protection.** The rental-price pair is at most 2 of the 4 the scaled count needs (22 to 24 of 26). None of the six
right refusals is a refusal for theme coverage, so a change of what the themes carry would not by itself turn them into
questions; the three other topics declined for coverage (a lidar ban, the CPU-to-GPU ratio in inference, Huawei's chip output)
have never been read for whether they are worth a question.

**Answer: no candidate.** The records establish a mechanism for one of the two matters, and for that one the change is a
product definition already put to Alex and stopped by a council decision, worth at most half the gap, with nothing on record
that the recovered question would receive sound choices or matter to a judgement. For the other matter no permitted change
exists. On the stored evidence the count by written choices is not reachable by a permitted change to the answer-choice step:
its distance is set upstream, by the topics the first step opens (rightly refused ones, and the memory shapes).

## 3. What follows (D549, D550)

The council accepted "no candidate" for the question asked, with two limits: the four recoveries are paper estimates, and the
record does not prove that no future change is possible. The state of the first gate on news outside the tuned days is
unknown (July: three runs over the same fourteen days; the fresh week: seven topics, no refusal), so the next step is a
measurement, not a repair: one more week through the new system, read for its answer choices, as a diagnostic that passes
nothing ([design](second-week/DESIGN.md)).

## 7. What a reader of the product would notice, beyond the lines

- No answer-choice question was written for the cloud companies' spending or for total AI spending. That both are worth a
  question is a reader's judgement (Claude's), not a measured result: the matching and the judge were not run.
- Topic 8 and topic 10 ask for an amount the article gives no figure for; the ranges are the step's guess and differ between
  attempts (a middle range of $5 to 10 billion in two attempts and $1 to 5 billion in the third; $8 to 12 an hour against $4
  to 6). This is the fault D546 recorded: the six lines do not see it.
- Topic 7's due day differs between attempts (February 28, February 24, February 28).
- The week has no library and no judgements: nothing here says how these questions would be answered.

## 8. What this is evidence of, and what it is not (design, section 6)

- **It is evidence that** on a second week outside the tuned days the frozen step shows the faults July showed: refusals of
  topics a reader wants answered, a question that drops a name, parts left unlisted. With the fresh week, two weeks give
  opposite pictures of refusals (0 of 21 attempts; 9 of 39). For the two spending topics the shape the first step gave them
  (two years in one topic) explains the refusal under the present rule; it does not explain the other three refusals (the
  commitments topic decided by chance, the rental price's theme).
- **A left-out part, agreed by both families, on two more questions** (topics 1 and 3): under the design this is a lead. The
  earlier audit (D547) found a place in the request that could produce it (the instruction says to list every other part of
  "the topic's wording" and never says whether the `outcome` field is part of that wording); it did not show that this caused
  each omission, and these new ones have not yet been traced against their requests. This week 27 of the 30 written answers list at
  least one such part; the three that list none are the three agreed faults of line 2.
- **A topic declined:** a lead. Section 5 counts the reasons the step gave; the earlier boundary check of this class (D469,
  D470: a candidate that takes the first-named figure as the main one was rejected as wider than Alex's rule, and a blind
  reader found it risked joining separately tracked things) stands, and this result does not reopen it.
- **It is not** a measurement of a rate (two weeks, 20 topics, not independent draws), not a pass or a fail of Stage A (Alex's
  lines are on 44 topics), and not a reason by itself to reverse the direction (D544) or to reopen a stopped line.
- **Limits:** continued after a stall, one call sent twice, a changed wait and reduced limits between the parts; one run;
  7 of the ten strict-count topics were opened in the week's first two days; the exposure search works by article id; the reading's
  third readers disagree on most of what was put to them, which is a finding about the form as much as about the answers.

item.text:
**I agree the next step is the $0 map, with two corrections: keep overlapping causes, and do not use the map alone to declare the gate unreachable.**

The [boundary study](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/NO-MAIN-BOUNDARY-STUDY.md) supports **no candidate under the condition we set**. The earlier two-reader classifications match the [blind key](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/ladder-refusal/blind-key.json) and the two verdict files I checked; the source-worth judgments for the three new topics are correctly marked as yours. The two July guards were independently judged unworthy of a question. The candidates considered either violate D397, risk opening those guards, or are already stopped. That does not prove no future design exists.

I would soften two conclusions in the study:

- **“The step draws the line where the readers draw it” is too broad.** The 27 of 27 refusals on the agreed no-main cases support it on those cases; 9 of 48 refusals on agreed one-main cases show the boundary is not consistently applied there.
- **“Two years in one topic is always a ‘none main’ topic” overstates the reading.** All nine stored attempts on the three identified topics were declined, but the two earlier readers split on whether `u1/clean-5` had a main part. Also, two worthwhile *matters* among 104 stored *topics* is a description of these cases, not a rate: the population includes repeated runs and different reading populations.

There is a correction to the premise for the map too. The original 44-topic Stage A was not about half right by written choices: its [fourth reading](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_a/result-4/RESULT.md) reported **31 of 44** on the favourable third-reader account and **25 of 44** on the strict one, against 28. The July and later-week results show a substantial gap, but the readings should remain separate, with their populations and disagreements visible.

For the **one next step**, map all 104 stored topics from the existing readings, at **$0 and with no sends**. For every topic that lacks two right written answers or has an agreed zero-fault mark, show the actual attempts, the marks and rulings, and the relevant decisions. Keep each run distinct, but identify repeated matters. Reconcile the map to each original report before drawing conclusions.

A topic can have **more than one cause or an unresolved cause**. For instance, an unworthy topic may be opened upstream and then correctly refused downstream; forcing it into one owner would conceal the interaction. Show which changes are only hypothetical, which are stopped, and which could overlap in the same recovered topic. Do not count an answerable but unworthy question as a recovery.

The map can identify a **credible bounded direction for the council to consider**, or show that the stored record contains no such direction. It cannot by itself prove the gate is impossible on future topics, establish that a proposed change would work, or trigger D544’s reversal. If it finds no credible direction, the council should then set and argue the promised bound against both the rebuild’s remaining gates and the alternative.

Record the annual-date note conflict alongside the map, as proposed. Preserve the original marks and distinguish the yearly-figure cases D414 addresses from the event and point-in-time disputes it does not.

Position: Continue the new system; make the $0 map with overlapping and unresolved causes, then decide from its evidence whether a bounded repair direction exists.
